limitations: A size-matched map-class retention contrast does NOT control photographic detection, phenology, water depth, patch shape or plant demographic survival.
Source polygons are spatially dependent; no p values or independent observational replicates are inferred.
The 5km grid is based on representative point of each source polygon; large polygons cross grid cells, so the grid is only a coarse geographic common-support screen.
Both class aggregation (patchy+continuous seagrass) and strict original FLUCCS code are reported to expose categorical coarsening.
If common-support algae area <80%, do not generalize to entire algae mapped footprint.
Same region, same remote sensing agency, post-hoc; not independent external validation.

explicit_scientific_conclusions: Before adjustment, sea and attached-algae same-broad-map-class retention differ by +53.902 percentage points.
Class-specific size distribution matters: the two source algae polygons >=50 acres account for about 46% of 2022 mapped algae area and have 16.518% same-class retention.

On the source-area common support in 4 fixed size bins (53.651% of algae area), sea vs algae standardized retention rates are 80.694% vs 53.508%, +27.186 points. Do not generalize to unmatched large algae polygons.

On size-bin + 5km representative-point grid support (47.288% of algae area), the descriptive difference is +8.020 points: sea 61.861%, algae 53.841%. This is CONDITIONAL on a minority of algae area, not a classwide adjusted result.
Strict same original FLUCCS classification is 78.877% for 2022 sea rather than 90.266% for patchy-plus-continuous combined, showing that category aggregation matters.

Neither mapped class contrasts nor strata establish biological survival, competition, or a causal algae effect; map detectability, source patch geometry, imagery dates, and spatial autocorrelation remain unresolved.
